# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28 (Bi-Vb Pc28)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28, titled *Cīvaradāna* ("Giving a robe to a non-monastic"), proscribes a Buddhist nun from giving robe material meant for an ascetic (*samaṇa*) to a householder (*gahapati*), a male wanderer (*paribbājaka*), or a female wanderer (*paribbājikā*) on pain of an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Bechert et al. 1997; Hüsken 1997]. In the rule's narrative origin story (*nidāna*), the nun Thullanandā gives robe material intended for a *samaṇa* to performers—including actors, dancers, and acrobats [Hüsken 1997]. The text's word commentary (*padabhājanīya*) defines a *paribbājaka* as anyone who has attained the status of a religious wanderer other than Buddhist monks (*bhikkhu*) and novices (*sāmaṇera*) [Bechert et al. 1997].
There is no direct parallel rule in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, although Buddhaghosa's *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī* notes that similar conduct is prohibited for monks [Hüsken 1997]. Across Buddhist monastic lineages, SuttaCentral lists full parallels in the Bhikkhunī Vinayas and Pātimokkhas of the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 107*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 87*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 132*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese *Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 142* and Tibetan *xct-mu-bi-vb-pc146*), Mahāsāṃghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc 72*), and Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc72*), as well as the Pali *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 298 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 81 texts, recording its largest formulaic overlaps with Bhikkhunī Pācittiyas 46, 81, 53, 48, 47, and 27 [DharmaNexus]. An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
